rationale: uswin-claude-agentic: train_n=800, val_n=200, epochs=40, batch_size=1, lr=0.0002, uswin_c=32, swin_window=8, swin_heads=8, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=ITER-13. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) READ iter-1..12: hr .649/.8193/.8092/.8208/.8136/.8093/.8440/.8464(c32bs1 tn200)/.8289(c48)/.8378(ep64)/.6059(lr3e-4 crash)/.8615(tn400,NEW BEST). iter-12 train_n 200->400 = 0.861475 ssim=0.9986 PSNR=53.49 RMSE=7.22e-4, backstop at ep26 (vs iter-8's 40 at tn200). +0.0151 hr DESPITE 14 fewer epochs -> U-Swin was strongly DATA-LIMITED at tn200; 2x data improved val generalization enough to beat the 40-epoch tn200 result. Loss ~5.9e-7 (deep, stable). Data is the dominant lever now. (2) FAILURE MODE / limiter: DATA VOLUME. iter-12 proved more scenes help a lot. Test whether the data-scaling continues: does 800 keep improving, or does the backstop epoch-cut (tn800 at bs1 = 800 steps/epoch, ~2x tn400 cost -> backstop ~ep13) finally outweigh the data gain? (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 400 -> 800 (2x again, <=2400 cap; 3600 available); hold everything else at iter-12 config (c32, bs=1, ep=40, lr=2e-4, win=8, heads=8, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). (4) HYPOTHESIS: U-Swin is still data-limited; train_n 400->800 continues the data-driven gain (diminishing but positive) and lifts hr above 0.8615, even though the backstop cuts epochs to ~13, because iter-12 showed the data effect dominates the epoch effect in this regime. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.8615 at tn800, the backstop epoch-cut (~ep13) now outweighs the data gain, i.e. tn400/ep26 is the budget-optimal data/epoch balance -> iter-14 either (a) reverts to tn400 and spends the extra budget on epochs (isolate: tn400 is proven, push its epochs), or (b) tries tn600 as a middle point. (5) 20-min budget via max_train_s=1000 backstop; val_n=200; train_n=800<=2400; expandable_segments OOM-guard. (6) STRICT SERIAL: rm iter-13 obs pre-dispatch; iter_wait.sh gate before iter-14.
